hero.eyebrow: Free, friendly tech help in New York City
hero.title2: What can we figure out together?
hero.description: If you have a security camera, video doorbell, Wi-Fi connection, or another device around the home that needs setting up or figuring out, feel free to ask. I’ve worked with technology for many years, and when we can find a time that works, I’m happy to come by and take a look with you.
hero.noCatch: It doesn’t have to be an installation or a technical problem, either. If you’re stuck on a computer, an online form, or something on your phone, small questions are welcome, too.
hero.pilotDescription: I offer my time freely because I enjoy helping. Sundays are usually when I have some time, so tell me what’s going on and we’ll see what works for both of us.

smallQuestions.title: Small Questions Are Always Welcome
smallQuestions.description1: Sometimes the hardest part is simply not having someone nearby to ask.
smallQuestions.description2: Maybe a security camera needs to be connected, a video doorbell isn’t working as expected, or the Wi-Fi doesn’t reach part of your home. Or perhaps you need help filling out an online form, attaching a document to an email, or figuring out something confusing on your phone or computer. You may wonder, “Is this too small to ask about?”
smallQuestions.description3: You don’t need to be good with technology or feel embarrassed about asking. Sometimes it just helps to have someone sit with you and work through it.
smallQuestions.closing: Just tell me what you’re trying to do. You don’t have to know the technical words.

about.title: A Little About Me
about.description1: I came to the United States from Korea in my twenties, and I’ve now lived and worked in New York and New Jersey for more than 30 years.
about.description2: When I stop and think about it, I’ve spent more of my life here than I did in Korea. This really is home to me.
about.career2: For many years, I ran technology businesses here—first NeoCymax in New York and later Multizer in New Jersey. I helped people and small businesses with computers, Wi-Fi, security cameras (CCTV), and video doorbells. Those years taught me a lot about solving everyday problems, including the little ones that can be surprisingly frustrating.
about.purpose1: Life hasn’t always gone as planned, but I’ve learned something about myself: helping someone with even a small problem can make my day, too.
about.purpose2: Call it joy, purpose, or maybe even a little dopamine—but I’ve never forgotten the feeling of seeing someone light up because I was able to help. I enjoy that feeling, and I’d like more of those moments in my life. So when I have the time and energy, this is something I like to do.
about.invitation: If there’s something I can safely help with, I’ll be glad to take a look. If it’s outside my experience, I’ll be honest and try to point you in the right direction.
about.quote: If helping someone makes their day a little easier and mine a little happier, that feels like a pretty good way to spend a Sunday.

communitySupport.eyebrow: A little help from good people
communitySupport.title: A Thank-You to Star Delta Electric
communitySupport.description2: I know the team at Star Delta Electric through my project work. When I told them what I wanted to do here, they kindly offered to volunteer their time and electrical expertise, too.
communitySupport.description3: I’m really grateful they offered to lend a hand. It means I have people I can turn to when a neighbor needs help with an electrical problem.
communitySupport.electricalDescription1: If you have an electrical problem—a light, outlet, switch, doorbell, or something else you’re not sure about—please feel free to ask.
communitySupport.electricalDescription2: Tell me what’s happening, even if you’re not sure what’s wrong. If it needs an electrician, I can help connect you with Star Delta and work out with them what help is possible and when.
communitySupport.electricalDescription3: If a permit, material cost, or work beyond the volunteer scope is required, we’ll explain everything clearly before anything moves forward.

trust.title: Before a Visit
trust.description: It’s natural to want to know a little about someone before inviting them in. We’ll talk first so you and your family can feel comfortable.
items: We’ll confirm the request, location, and appointment details before I visit.
I’m happy to show a photo ID when I arrive.
I will never ask for your banking information or ask you to tell me a private password.
A family member, friend, or caregiver is always welcome to be present.

stories.title: Stories from My Sunday Visits
stories.emptyNote: There aren’t any stories posted here yet. I hope to use this space for small moments from my Sunday visits—the things we figure out together and what I learn along the way.

howToApply.title: Tell Me What’s Going On
howToApply.description: You can call and leave me a voicemail, or send an email—whichever feels easier. Just tell me:
howToApply.phoneLabel: Call Kenny and Leave a Message
howToApply.voicemailNote: I work during the week, so I usually can’t answer the phone. If I don’t pick up, please leave your name, phone number, and a little about what you need help with. I’ll check your message and get back to you when I can. There’s no need to explain everything perfectly.
howToApply.onBehalf: A family member, friend, or neighbor is welcome to contact me on your behalf. You can also get in touch for someone who could use a hand—with their permission.
howToApply.serviceAreaTitle: Where and When I Can Help
howToApply.serviceAreaMessage: I can visit Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn on Sundays by arrangement. Let me know your neighborhood so we can work out whether and when I can visit.
howToApply.step1: Your name and what you would like help with
howToApply.step3: The best phone number or email for reaching you
howToApply.availability: This fits around my work and everyday life, so I won’t always be available. Feel free to ask, and we’ll see if we can find a time that works for both of us.

contact.wantToHelp: Want to join me on a Sunday?
contact.volunteerDescription: If you’re a kind, patient person who would like to share some time or a useful skill with a neighbor, feel free to get in touch using the contact information above.

footer.disclaimer: This is Kenny’s personal volunteer project and is not a registered nonprofit.
